title: Realtime conversation events
description: Conversation event streams opened through the SDK's subscribe/watch API: replay then live delivery as one ordered run, agreement between subscribers, visibility for late members, reconnect after a server restart or gateway errors and as close reasons direct (spec/recovery/README.md#retry-and-reconnect), resume from a persisted cursor and authorization failures. Event type strings are not pinned; events are identified by sequence, subjectRef and payload.

scenarios.title: A subscriber receives retained history and then live events as one gap-free, duplicate-free ascending run

steps.note: The first event alice may read. The stream must start from the same place.
Replay delivers everything already retained, oldest first.
Live events continue the same run with no gaps or repeats.

scenarios.title: Two members watching the same conversation see the same events in the same order

steps.note: Authors receive their own messages as events too.

scenarios.title: Edits and deletes arrive as new events carrying the message's new revision

steps.note: The edit is a new event at the message's revisionSequence; the original event is not rewritten.

scenarios.title: A member added later receives no events from before it joined

steps.note: The stream starts where carol's readable history starts, which is never before visibleFromSequence.

scenarios.title: After a server restart the SDK resubscribes on its own from its cursor and misses nothing sent while it was away
scenarios.description: The target closes the socket with 1012 (service restart). Events sent while disconnected must be delivered once, in order, and the new subscription must resume after the last applied event rather than replay from the start.

steps.note: Wait until the realtime subscription is registered so the restart hits a live socket.
No application call is involved: the SDK reconnects by itself and subscribes after the last event it applied.
SDKs may report transient errors while reconnecting, but the stream must stay open.

scenarios.title: When the server ends a subscription's authorization the stream closes with UNAUTHENTICATED and does not reconnect
scenarios.description: The target closes the socket with graphql-transport-ws 4401, as it does when a session expires or is revoked. Reconnecting with the same credential would only fail again.

steps.note: Longer than any first reconnect delay.
Still exactly one subscription: the SDK did not retry with the rejected credential.

scenarios.title: A reconnect that meets 502 and then 504 keeps retrying with backoff instead of ending the stream
scenarios.description: Every reconnect attempt routes again first. Here the first two route calls fail with plain-text gateway errors; a 5xx is retryable like a network failure, so the stream keeps reconnecting (spec/recovery/README.md#retry-and-reconnect).

steps.note: The first reconnect attempt met 502; the second, after a longer backoff, met 504.
The third attempt routes and subscribes again.
SDKs may report the gateway errors, but the stream must stay open.

scenarios.title: A rate-limited reconnect attempt waits at least its Retry-After before the next one
scenarios.description: The second reconnect attempt would come after about two seconds; the RATE_LIMITED answer's six-second Retry-After is a floor on that backoff.

steps.note: The first reconnect attempt is rate limited.
Longer than the next backoff without Retry-After (at most 2.5 seconds), shorter than Retry-After.
Still one subscription: the SDK is waiting out Retry-After.
Then it reconnects by itself.

scenarios.title: A RATE_LIMITED close reconnects, but no sooner than the retryAfter in its reason
scenarios.description: The service closes a rate-limited subscription with 4429 and the reason "RATE_LIMITED retryAfter=N". The error code in the reason decides whether to reconnect, not the close code alone, and retryAfter is a floor on the backoff.

steps.note: Longer than the first reconnect delay without retryAfter (at most 1.5 seconds), shorter than retryAfter.
Still one subscription: the SDK is waiting out retryAfter.
Then it reconnects by itself.

scenarios.title: A QUOTA_EXCEEDED close ends the stream and reports the quota instead of reconnecting
scenarios.description: The service closes with 4429 and the reason "QUOTA_EXCEEDED retryAfter=N meter=M". Unlike RATE_LIMITED, a spent quota is not retryable: the app decides what to do.

steps.note: Longer than any first reconnect delay.
Still exactly one subscription.

scenarios.title: A PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED close ends the stream with that code rather than UNAUTHENTICATED
scenarios.description: The service closes with 4403 and the reason "PLAN_LIMIT_EXCEEDED planLimit=X". 4403 ends the stream either way, but the code in the reason tells the app what to change.

steps.note: Longer than any first reconnect delay.
Still exactly one subscription.

scenarios.title: A restarted client with the same storage resumes after its persisted cursor
scenarios.description: Only events after the last applied cursor are delivered after a restart; nothing already applied is replayed.

scenarios.title: Subscribing to a conversation the principal is not a member of fails as NOT_FOUND

steps.note: Existence is not disclosed to non-members.

scenarios.title: Subscribing with an invalid session token fails as UNAUTHENTICATED
